title: Presentation Model

validation.research: Five primary sources: Fowler’s Presentation Model catalog entry, Gossman’s original MVVM introduction archived by Microsoft, and official Microsoft documentation on MVVM, WPF binding source-update timing, and RelayCommand availability notification. Fowler explicitly lists MVVM as another name; the article uses one canonical record, explains the binding-oriented realization, and distinguishes MVC/MVP and accepted domain state. The Python example is an explicit synchronization implementation rather than a claimed WPF or MAUI binding engine.

example_limits: Original sequential in-memory profile editing session. Profile owns a trimmed 1–40 Unicode-code-point name and independently validates rename before assignment. ProfileEditor owns raw drafts, feedback, derived Apply/Cancel availability, and actions without any view reference. Invalid Apply leaves accepted state unchanged; successful Apply normalizes and accepts the draft; Cancel reloads the current domain value, not an initial snapshot or save rollback. The console view explicitly pulls properties after each interaction and prints the domain name only as diagnostic evidence. No GUI, binding engine, change notification, async service, persistence, authorization, or concurrent-edit protection is implemented. A search-screen second context illustrates stale completion policy but is not runnable search code.
